This is a seminar course where we will discuss and analyze research papers, and solve problems as assignments, and there will be presentations of the papers.  
Proteins are fascinating molecular machines that carry out every function inside the cells whose properties are so useful that we employ them as therapeutic agents, catalysts, and materials. Many diseases stem from protein mutations impairing their folding, structure, or activity. This course will discuss the physical chemistry of protein molecules. This course is for students of Biological Sciences who are comfortable with mathematics. This is also a course for chemistry and physics students who want to think about proteins.
Associate Professor, Biological Sciences and Chemistry
